# MSBuild Code Review Report

**Scope:** 2 C# projects (LibA, LibB), 2 F# projects (BrokenOrder, OrderService), root `Directory.Build.props`/`.targets`, F# subfolder `Directory.Build.props`/`.targets`, solution file.

---

## 🔴 Errors (will cause build failures or incorrect behavior)

### 1. `Directory.Build.props` — `$(TargetFramework)` condition is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props:10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```
**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this repo), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK sets it later during the outer-build → inner-build dispatch. This condition never matches, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set.

**Fix:** Move TFM-conditional **property** logic to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is evaluated after the SDK has resolved the target framework:
```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 2. `Directory.Build.targets` — Property defaults override project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets:6-10`
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```
**Problem:** `.targets` is imported **after** the project file. MSBuild uses last-write-wins for properties. This means every project gets `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` regardless of what they set locally. LibB explicitly sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>` (line 13), but it is silently overridden back to `true` by this file.

**Fix:** Move default properties that projects should be able to override into `Directory.Build.props` with a conditional guard:
```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```
This sets them as defaults that individual projects can override.

---

### 3. `LibA.csproj` — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:13-14`
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
  <DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```
**Problem (two issues):**

**(a)** Assignment **overwrites** instead of appending. The SDK sets `TRACE` (and `DEBUG` in Debug configuration) by default. This kills all of them, replacing them with only `ENABLE_LOGGING`. Code guarded by `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` will silently stop compiling.

**(b)** The `Condition` is **unquoted**: `$(Configuration) == Debug`. If `$(Configuration)` is ever empty, this evaluates to `== Debug` which is a malformed expression. MSBuild tolerates this today but it's fragile.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
  <DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 4. `LibA.csproj` — Redundant `Compile Include` causes duplicate CS2002
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:21-22`
```xml
<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />
<Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
```
**Problem:** SDK-style projects auto-glob all `*.cs` files. The explicit `Include` adds a **second** entry for `Class1.cs`, producing a `CS2002` duplicate-source warning (or error with `TreatWarningsAsErrors`). The `Update` in the same `ItemGroup` as the `Include` also has subtle evaluation-order concerns.

**Fix:** Remove the `Include` and keep only the `Update`:
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Update="Class1.cs" AutoGen="true" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 5. `LibA.csproj` — Publish-on-build re-enters the project (AP-22)
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:43-45`
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```
**Problem:** This forks a **second evaluation** of the same project with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). The two instances share the same `OutputPath` / `IntermediateOutputPath`, so they race writing identical files. This causes intermittent "file in use" failures and doubles build time.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` or `CallTarget` to invoke Publish within the **same** project instance, with a guard property to prevent infinite recursion:
```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build"
        Condition="'$(_IsPublishing)' != 'true'">
  <CallTarget Targets="Publish" />
</Target>
```
Or better, run `dotnet publish` instead of `dotnet build` when publishing is needed.

---

### 6. `BrokenOrder.fsproj` — F# compile order is wrong
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj:7-9`
```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```
**Problem:** F# compilation is **order-dependent** — files can only reference types from files listed above them. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain` (defined in `Domain.fs`), but `Domain.fs` is listed *after* `Services.fs`. This will fail with a compile error.

Compare with `OrderService.fsproj` which correctly lists `Domain.fs` before `Services.fs`.

**Fix:**
```xml
<ItemGroup>
  <Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Services.fs" />
  <Compile Include="Program.fs" />
</ItemGroup>
```

---

## 🟡 Warnings (anti-patterns that should be fixed)

### 7. `LibA.csproj` & `LibB.csproj` — Hardcoded Windows `OutputPath`
**Files:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:7`, `LibB/LibB.csproj:7`
```xml
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibA</OutputPath>
<OutputPath>C:\builds\output\LibB</OutputPath>
```
**Problem:** Absolute Windows paths break on Linux/macOS and tie the build to a specific machine layout. They also break the SDK's default incremental build logic which expects outputs under `bin/`.

**Fix:** Use relative paths or SDK-standard conventions:
```xml
<OutputPath>bin\$(Configuration)\</OutputPath>
```
Or remove entirely to use SDK defaults.

### 8. `LibA.csproj` — Legacy `<Reference>` with HintPath to packages folder
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj:27-29`
```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```
**Problem:** This is a `packages.config`-style reference in an SDK-style project. The `packages/` folder won't exist with `PackageReference` restore. This reference will resolve only if the DLL happens to be at that path — it's fragile and skips NuGet's TFM resolution.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper `PackageReference`:

<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

**File:** `Directory.Build.props:17`

<PackageReference Include="StyleCop.Analyzers" Version="1.2.0-beta.556" />
